sentences.text: Aardonyx is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur named from Afrikaans for "earth" and Greek for "nail or claw". The genus is known from the remains of two immature individuals. Both fossil individuals are estimated to have been under 10 years old when they died.

The species Aardonyx celestae was named in honor of Celeste Yates, who prepared most of the initial fossil material. The genus was discovered by Australian paleontologist Adam Yates and his team, with findings published online in November 2009 and in print in March 2010. Aardonyx celestae is known from the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation in South Africa.

Aardonyx was primarily bipedal but capable of moving on all fours like Iguanodon. Aardonyx had a slower gait compared to more basal sauropodomorphs. Aardonyx was a powerful but slow walker due to a distal fourth trochanter that increased muscle leverage but reduced retraction speed. Aardonyx exhibited entaxony, indicating reduced running ability and a wide gait that preceded the full quadrupedalism of later sauropods.

Aardonyx grew rapidly with growth patterns that were seasonally interrupted. Aardonyx displayed a transition toward the bulk-browsing feeding style characteristic of sauropods. Aardonyx lacked fleshy cheeks, an adaptation for a wider mouth opening to facilitate bulk browsing.
Aardonyx is classified as the sister taxon to a clade containing Melanorosaurus and sauropods.
Aardonyx lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
It is debated whether the wide, cheekless gape evolved independently in Aardonyx and in later sauropods, as suggested by the more derived state of Chinshakiangosaurus.
